_comment: Golden cases for the LIVE screening eval (app/evals/screening.py). Each case is a real SYNTHETIC applicant (exact slice from the pool), run through the REAL production screening prompt+model. Screening produces (1) a LIST of integrity flags and (2) an extracted PET inventory. The grade is per-CATEGORY for flags — metadata.expected.fires = categories that MUST appear; metadata.expected.absent = categories that must NOT (the over-reach guards — flagging benign things is the costly error since flags gate eligibility) — PLUS, when metadata.expected.pets is set, the extracted pet facts must match (dogs/cats exact; each other_pets noun present). Pets are NO LONGER a flag (M15 1e): the model only EXTRACTS the neutral inventory, and a deterministic per-member hard filter judges the limits downstream — so a pet case grades extraction, never a pet_policy verdict. A clean applicant (no fires, no absent, no pets expectation) must produce zero flags. given.fields (normalized form fields) + given.essays (keyed by the real form-question column) are what the screening prompt receives; metadata is harness-only. See docs/eval-case-schema.md.
judge_background: Screening reviews an applicant's fields and essays for INFORMATIONAL integrity concerns — never disqualifying, only surfaced for a human to review — and separately EXTRACTS a neutral inventory of the household's pets. Flag genuine concerns such as: internal inconsistencies between fields/essays; placeholder or fake contact details (keyboard-mash emails, obviously bogus phone numbers); and placeholder names (e.g. a child named 'TBD'). Pets are NEVER a flag: report what animals are present (dogs, cats, other) and let the committee's per-member policy decide — account for negation like 'no pets' and unclear phrasing when counting. The following must not be flagged: a child with a different surname, an email address with a full name in it that doesn't match someone in the household. The cases you must not flag do not indicate a fake contact.

metadata.note: EXTRACTION: 'Two dogs and a cat' must be counted as dogs=2, cats=1, no others. (Pre-1e this was a pet_policy flag; pets are now extracted facts and the per-member filter judges the 1-dog/1-cat limit downstream.)

We'd bring reliability, an ethic of care, and the kind of neighbourliness that turns a building into a place people don't want to leave.

metadata.note: CONTESTED essay-flag axis + fake_contact over-reach guard. The intro essay is vapid corporate word-salad ('leveraging synergies … to drive meaningful, value-added community outcomes'), BUT it's one grammatical, on-topic sentence and the other three essays are substantive and sincere (nurse, CPR station, tool library) — so this is a weak-but-genuine answer, not a spam/bot application. Whether that glib sentence is a flaggable integrity concern (spam/minimal/ai_generated) or just a weak essay the committee judges itself is a defensible tone/quality call either way — the prompt's north star is 'flag only concrete, clear problems.' So the essay-flag axis is left UNGRADED (in neither fires nor absent): fire or not, both pass; stability on it isn't required. The case still grades the pet extraction and guards the name/email mismatch. (History: first added as a must-fire spam_essay regression case after it silently de-flagged; reclassified contested 2026-07-24 on reflection — it straddles three categories without cleanly landing in any.) Also carries a name/email mismatch (morganchen@ for Emerson Delgado) that must NOT fire fake_contact.
